messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Targets different behavior with cross-loading
parts:
Ed

I was doing some testing for a next simulation, and found that target "stan" and "stanclassic" dont produce the same results with cross-loadings with small prior variances.

So I generated data with a cross-loading = 0.2. Then run the model with the respective cross-loadings with a small variance prior, with target "stan" and "stanclassic".
Target "stan" seems to identify the missed parameter should not have the small variance priors, and biased another factor loading. This is kind of what I was expecting
Target "stanclassic" still see the cross-loading as small effect, and doesnt affect the other factor loadings

I was expecting both methods to have similar behavior. Am I missing something about why they are getting these different results?

Here is the basic code, and results. You can download the workspace from these results here https://www.dropbox.com/s/t5nmtlov8kcume3/test_target_cl.RData?dl=0

Thanks

###############
###############
library(blavaan)
library(simsem)

N <- 1000
Nreps <- 2000
rep <- 2000
CL <- 0.2

###############
#### simulate data with simsem
###############
loading <- matrix(0, 8, 2) #create a matrix of all 0s
loading[1:4, 1] <- NA #specify free parameters with NA
loading[5:8, 2] <- NA
loading[3, 2] <- NA #### cross-loading, item 3 on factor 2

loadingValues <- matrix(0, 8, 2) 
loadingValues[1:4, 1] <- 0.7 
loadingValues[5:8, 2] <- 0.7
loadingValues[3, 2] <- CL

LY <- bind(loading, loadingValues)
LY
summary(LY)

error.cor <- matrix(0, 8, 8)
diag(error.cor) <- 1
RTE <- binds(error.cor)

latent.cor <- matrix(NA, 2, 2) #specify a 2x2 matrix of NAs
diag(latent.cor) <- 1 #set the diagonal of the matrix to 1
RPS <- binds(latent.cor, 0.3) #Defaults to making all NA values in the matrix .5

CFA.Model <- model(LY = LY, RPS = RPS, RTE = RTE, modelType="CFA")
summary(CFA.Model)

dat <- generate(CFA.Model, N)
head(dat)
###
mod_test_2 <- '
f1 =~ y1+y2+y3+y4
f2 =~ y5+y6+y7+y8 + prior("normal(0,.01)")*y3
'

#### stan
rhat <- 20
brn <- 3000
while(rhat > 1.05){
  brn <- brn + 3000
  bfit_stan <- bcfa(mod_test_2, data = dat, std.lv=T,target="stan",
               n.chains = 3, burnin = brn, sample = 2000)
  print(rhat <- max(blavInspect(bfit_stan, "psrf")))
}



#### stanclassic
rhat <- 20
brn <- 3000
while(rhat > 1.05){
  brn <- brn + 3000
  bfit_stan_cl <- bcfa(mod_test_2, data = dat, std.lv=T,target="stanclassic",
                    n.chains = 3, burnin = brn, sample = 2000)
  print(rhat <- max(blavInspect(bfit_stan_cl, "psrf")))
}



summary(bfit_stan)
summary(bfit_stan_cl)

messages.subject: Re: Targets different behavior with cross-loading
parts: ####JAGS
Estimate  Post.SD  HPD.025  HPD.975     PSRF    Prior
f2 =~
y3                0.180    0.028    0.125    0.234    1.001   dnorm(0,1/.01)

JAGS takes precision as inverse of prior variance, right?  I thought target="stan" expected prior SDs (square-root of variance), since that is the (correct!!!) parameter specification that Stan uses.  But it looks like you specified normal(0, .01) with both Stan targets.  Perhaps StanClassic is treating that is as the prior SD (in which case you would want to pass normal(0, .1) instead) whereas the new target is treating that as prior variance?  Just a speculation, I haven't had time to investigate (and I forget what blavaan's documentation says), but it would be consistent with the much narrower posterior returned by stanclassic.

Terrence D. Jorgensen

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Targets different behavior with cross-loading
parts:
I think the prior specifications are ok: for normal priors, jags always takes precision, and any Stan target always takes SD.

I think this is a bug in target="stan", and I am currently testing a fix.

Ed
